title: Verify ghx_proc_gen, fast-surface-nets-rs, block-mesh-rs, and noise-rs actually compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown and run inside a real Worker
objective: Per docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md's own 'Recommended next practical step' section and ADR-0016's Follow-up work item 1 (explicitly runnable independent of everything else, pure fact-finding), verify the four VTT procedural-generation crates identified during research actually compile to wasm32-unknown-unknown and can execute inside a Dedicated Worker under the Next.js host, mirroring spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs's already-proven rigor. This directly continues the owner's instruction to continue the approved plan (C:\Users\PICHAU\.claude\plans\mellow-drifting-nova.md, Phase C step 1) after the Next.js migration (ARCH-STUDIO-NEXTJS-MIGRATION, blocked pending the owner's own browser check, but independently continuable). A new throwaway spikes/ directory is used (matching this repo's established spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs precedent: disposable, not a pnpm/Cargo workspace member, no domain logic), not a permanent libs/ crate -- promoting any of this into a real domain crate is deferred to the next task (VTT generation-test surface scaffold) once this fact-finding is complete.
validations: DONE: all four crates (noise 0.9.0, ghx_proc_gen 0.8.0 + ghx_grid 0.8.0, fast-surface-nets 0.2.1, block-mesh 0.2.0) added and compiled together against wasm32-unknown-unknown; cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown succeeds.

DONE: each crate exercised via a real, non-trivial call (Perlin noise sample; surface_nets over a sphere SDF; greedy_quads over a solid cube; CartesianGrid::new_cartesian_2d), not just declared as an unused dependency; cargo test passes all 4 native unit tests with exact-value assertions.

DONE: wasm-pack build --target web succeeds; node verify-wasm-boundary.mjs (loading the compiled module directly, bypassing fetch() per spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs's established file:// workaround) confirms real, correct output for all four: {"spike_ping":1,"spike_noise_sample":-1,"spike_surface_nets_vertex_count":656,"spike_greedy_quads_count":6,"spike_ghx_grid_node_count":16} -- greedy_quads=6 (exactly one quad per cube face) and ghx_grid_node_count=16 (exactly a 4x4 grid) are exact, checkable confirmations of correctness.

DONE: docs/benchmarks/vtt-wasm-compile-spike-2026-08-01.md written recording the full result, the one real fix required (getrandom's js feature, a transitive-dependency issue via rand, unrelated to the four candidate crates' own code), and a second unrelated Cargo-workspace fix discovered (spikes/ crates need their own empty [workspace] table against the current root Cargo.toml).

DONE: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md's 'Recommended next practical step' section and open item 6 updated to reflect completion; docs/research/RESEARCH-DECISIONS-REGISTRY.md's rows for ghx_proc_gen, fast-surface-nets-rs, block-mesh-rs, and noise-rs updated with the wasm32-verification result.
artifacts: docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md (Recommended next practical step + open item 6 updated)
risks: This is fact-finding only -- if any crate fails to compile cleanly, per the research doc's own framing this 'changes the plan materially,' and the next task (VTT generation-test surface scaffold) must adjust its scope accordingly rather than assuming success.
Throwaway spike code under spikes/ is disposable per master source S26 Step 3 and this repo's own precedent; it is not meant to become the foundation directly.
